fact_check.claim: 'this is a 95 million right now... almost like a 30x at this point... my lowest entry was a four million market cap... you might have caught it at a 2.9 million' (transcript, on EVAA)

At stream time (Nov 19 to 20) $EVAA traded around $5.20; CoinMarketCap's self-reported circulating supply (17.85M) makes that around $95M, while CoinGecko's circulating supply (6.62M) makes it around $34M. The low market caps are CoinGecko-basis figures: $2.7M to $4.0M on many days in March, April, June and October 2026 (price $0.41 to $0.60; all-time low $0.2818 on June 5 2026). So '30x' is $95M on one supply figure over $2.9M to $4M on the other. On price it was around 9x to 12x at stream time. Copy prints dated prices only: 51 cents on October 27 2026 (CoinGecko daily $0.5101) to above $6.60 on November 21 (CoinGecko hourly high $6.62 at 09:00 UTC) = 12.97x, written 'around 13x in under four weeks' (25 days, my calc). 'My lowest entry was near a $4 million market cap' and 'days it traded under $3 million' are Mike's own entries and match the CoinGecko series. OPERATOR NOTE: ask Mike which multiple he wants on record before a '30x' goes into any copy.

Checked: evaa.finance (tagline only), token.evaa.finance (search result), api.llama.fi/protocol/evaa-protocol (200), /protocol/evaa and /protocol/evaa-finance (not found). The longform dossier ran the full telemetry sweep two days earlier: every standard path on the site returns the app shell, the project API exposes supply and price but no user, revenue or live TVL endpoint, and the home page's own counters ('300K+ unique wallets', '1.4B+ transaction volume', '118M+ total deposit at the peak') are hard-coded, undated project claims. yt_posts.topic: Kaspa has no spot listing on Binance or Coinbase and is still a top 100 coin: where it trades, Mike's 2025 call, the fair launch reason, when the tier ones show up
yt_posts.body_style: stat hook, where it trades, the call, the fair launch reason, the play, the comment ask
yt_posts.body:
Kaspa is a top 100 coin with no spot listing on Binance and no spot listing on Coinbase. A viewer told me he expects the tier one listings in 2027. I think he's right, and the reason they've waited this long is the same reason I'm in it.

Start with where things stand. $KAS trades on Kraken, Bybit, Gate, MEXC, KuCoin and HTX. Binance has a futures market for it and no spot pair. Coinbase has no spot listing at all. In Europe it trades against the euro on Kraken and Bitvavo. With both of the big two missing, Kaspa still sits inside the top 100 by market cap, at around 2.6 cents, and it's doing that around 88% under its all-time high.

I've been saying this since the first half of 2025. Back when I dropped the four-year cycle idea, I said Kaspa wasn't getting listed on Binance spot or Coinbase for a long time. People didn't want to hear it. Some of them came after me for it. Look where we are: it's late 2026 and neither listing has happened.

Here's why. Kaspa was a fair launch. No premine, no presale, no insider allocation. That means there's no pile of free coins sitting anywhere to fund a listing. To me, the missing listings are the receipt that the launch was fair.

And the tier ones are businesses. They list what brings them volume, and that happens when the market is flying, not at the bottom. I don't expect them to show up while everything is down. I expect them to show up when Kaspa is already running and they can't ignore it anymore.

So what do you do with that? You can wait for the announcement and buy the listing pump with everybody else. Or you can do what I've been doing: buy the bottoms, on the exchanges that already have it, while the big ones are still on the sidelines. Never financial advice.

So tell me: who lists Kaspa first, Binance spot or Coinbase? And what year? Drop it in the comments.

If this helped you see the listing story differently, hit like and subscribe for more.

yt_posts.topic: The EVAA reveal: a TON lending protocol inside Telegram that ran around 13x in under four weeks and then dropped more than 50% in a day, how the call went, and why Mike takes profits on the way up (LAB and Velvet as precedent)
yt_posts.body_style: the reveal, what it is, how the call went, the run and the drop, the precedent, the comment ask
yt_posts.body:
On November 19 I revealed a play my community has been in for over a year. It ran around 13x in under four weeks. Then it dropped more than 50% in a single day. Both of those things are the lesson, so let me walk you through it.

The play is EVAA. It's the first lending protocol on TON, and it lives right inside Telegram: you open a mini app and you can lend, borrow and earn yield without leaving the chat. It's backed by TON Ventures, Animoca Brands and Polymorphic Capital. Telegram is a powerhouse, and that's why Gram, the old Toncoin, sits in my top three right behind Kaspa and TAO.

Here's how the call went. My bot flagged $EVAA around its launch in October 2025. It spiked, it came back down, and we kept buying the bottoms for a year. My lowest entry was near a $4 million market cap, and there were days it traded under $3 million.

Then it moved. On October 27 it was sitting at 51 cents. On November 21 it traded above $6.60. That's around 13x in 25 days, while Bitcoin fell more than 20% over the same stretch.

And on November 22 it dropped more than 50% in one day.

Here's the thing: I said that on stream before it happened. I said it could come right back down, that I had already taken profits on the way up, and that if it did come back down I would buy back in, because long term I expect this one over a $1 billion market cap.

You never know how far one of these runs. LAB is the one I always go back to. I expected a 20x and it did 353x, past a $7 billion market cap. Velvet ran a month later and topped out under $1 billion. Same kind of setup, completely different ending. That's why I sell some on the way up. Never financial advice.

So tell me: when a play runs 13x in a month, what do you do? Take profits on the way up, hold for the long run, or wait and buy the drop? Drop it in the comments.

If this helped you think about how these runs work, hit like and subscribe so you catch the next one.
